slides.reasoning: Design A delivers a bolder condensed-numeral hierarchy with a full-bleed rising chart, disciplined metric rules and a proof-point footer band, while Design B leaves a large dead zone under the left metrics and lets the '4.8' label crowd the plot edge.

Design A's illustrated route with numbered stops, staggered labels and a full three-column editorial breakdown fills the frame gracefully, whereas Design B leaves a big empty mid-band and has label text sitting on top of the dashed path near 'judgment'.

Design A shows a genuinely precise enterprise before/after with an identity-graph diagram, tiered ROI row and clean rules; Design B's two heavy blocks are internally under-filled and its metric row crowds unevenly against the CTA.

Design A's restrained serif voice, orbital allocation wheel and structured left column match the institutional brief better, while Design B's all-caps sans headline breaks the serif tone and leaves a large empty lower-right void.

Design A stages a cinematic keynote reveal with oversized wordmark, callout annotations and a graphite price bar, while Design B centers a small boxed stock render in a symmetrical four-label layout that reads as a brochure with visible letter-spacing glitches.

Design A's calm monospaced scorecard, variance callouts and hatched activation gap bar are tightly integrated, whereas Design B has the '103% of plan' label colliding with the dashed plan line and a very heavy orange footer that unbalances the palette.

Design A builds a true transit-map diagram with interchange spine, wayfinding labels and a north-star measures band, while Design B's four parallel straight rules feel diagrammatically flat, misassigns labels between lanes, and leaves a large empty gap above the footer.

Design A's phase bars, diamond gates and team/rollout footer are cleanly aligned with no overlaps, while Design B's gate labels overrun and collide with the phase bars (notably Gate C over the Build & Pilot block) in a spreadsheet-like Gantt.

Design A pairs a bold facilitation loop with a well-set worked-example panel and marker-style annotation, while Design B shows doubled quotation marks, a label overlapping the ring, and a large empty right-hand area.

Design A's editorial 68% figure, dot matrix, three-app handover chain and quote block are elegantly balanced, whereas Design B's headline wraps awkwardly onto a stray 'DECISIONS' line crowding the 68% and its stacked app boxes read generically.

Design A creates the auditorium-scale typographic moment with a layered oversized title and a clear visible/hidden UI diagram, while Design B's small title, awkward script-italic provocation and photo-half composition lack keynote presence and typographic discipline.

Design A confidently mixes oversized numbers, customer quote and three priorities across a full, well-margined field, while Design B leaves nearly a third of the orange panel empty and buries the closing line in a cramped sidebar list.

Design A makes the corridor map the emotional centerpiece with mapped milestones, scale bar and a tidy funding column, while Design B's schematic corridor overlaps its own km labels and leaves a large blank lower-right area.

Design A's letterform is larger and genuinely instructional with baseline/x-height rules and clean leader lines, while Design B's leader lines cross the glyph and each other, with the aperture label pointing awkwardly below the baseline.

Design A's collage of ingredient graphics, audience stacked bar and partnership moments fills the plum field energetically, while Design B has broken letter-spacing in its partnership chips ('FUT URE T ABLE ST AGE') and a large empty right-hand void.
